title: Phase 5 maintenance-window rehearsal: full PG backup preserves the credential-governance security ledger hash chain
purpose: Phase 5 window step 1 (docs/deployment/credential-security-operations.md §3) requires a full PG backup that preserves the append-only security ledger hash chain. This rehearsal proves a plain-format pg_dump, restored to a fresh database, keeps the chain cryptographically valid — re-verified with the real SecurityEventHash.Compute against the read-back rows.
whySeedViaSeeder: No production code path writes security_events at main HEAD: SecurityLeaseIssuer.IssueAsync is a closed 503 stub with no DI/endpoint wiring (P2-4 finding), and revocation/rotation only move credential status columns. So a scratch seeder builds a valid chain using the real SecurityEventHash.Compute and the real entities, satisfying the guard triggers (environment_security_initializations must be inserted as FreshNonStrict; environment_security_states genesis requires head_hash = Genesis).

environment.composeProject: webapi-enterprise-e2e-g13p5-1794151839 (disposable; torn down with volumes after the run)
environment.migratorAttempt: Migration attempt cab48714-3eee-4975-a3c6-e175eea323b1: Committed; reason=None (bare WebApi.Migrator, no bootstrap/seed — all 35 migrations applied to an empty DB)

seed.occurredAtPrecision: whole-second UTC (DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeMilliseconds); verify normalizes read-back to UTC before recomputing the hash, so the check is immune to Npgsql timestamptz offset rendering

backup.method: plain pg_dump -U webapi -d webapi (all 98 public tables) restored via psql into a fresh database webapi_restore

conclusion: A full plain-format pg_dump of a database holding a valid credential-governance security ledger restores with the hash chain byte-identical and still cryptographically valid (Genesis -> ... -> head). This satisfies the Phase 5 window backup requirement that the append-only ledger hash chain be preserved by the backup.
relationshipToP2_2: Orthogonal to P2-2, which showed a dump/restore round-trip is NOT schema-fingerprint-canonical (pg_dump re-serializes CHECK-constraint array literals, so the governance fingerprint preflight rejects dump-REBUILT schemas — hence the production pre-G -> G upgrade must run the G migrator directly, never dump/restore). Here the object under test is the ledger DATA (hash-chained rows) in an already-migrated, EF-created schema: that data path is canonical under plain backup/restore. A disaster-recovery restore of an already-G database re-creates the schema from the dump and re-creates the data; the ledger chain survives, and DR should start the G services against the restored DB rather than re-running the migration.
